verses.text: It's actually been reported that there's sexual immorality among you—so serious that even people outside the church don't do this: one man is living with his father's wife.
And you're proud? You should be grieving instead, so the person who did this would be removed from your community.
Though I'm away from you physically, I'm with you in spirit. I've already judged the person who did this, as if I were there.
When you gather in the name of our Lord Jesus, and my spirit is with you, act with the power of our Lord Jesus:
hand this person over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that their spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord Jesus.
Your bragging isn't good. Don't you know a little yeast spreads through the whole batch of dough?
Clear out the old yeast so you can be a fresh batch, as you really are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.
So let's celebrate—not with the old yeast of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people.
I didn't mean the sexually immoral people of this world, or the greedy, swindlers, or idol worshipers. You'd have to leave the world to avoid them all.

What I meant was: don't associate with anyone who claims to be a brother or sister but is sexually immoral, greedy, an idol worshiper, an abusive slanderer, a drunkard, or a swindler. Don't even share a meal with such a person.
Why should I judge people outside the church? Aren't you supposed to judge those inside?
God will judge those outside. As Scripture says, ‘Remove the evil person from among you.’
